highlights.title: Generative AI, Managerial Expectations, and Economic Activity
highlights.summary: Using GenAI to extract economic expectations from 120,000+ corporate conference call transcripts, the AI Economy Score predicts GDP growth, employment, and wages 5+ quarters ahead, outperforming survey forecasts; industry-level variation reveals heterogeneous labor market impacts.

highlights.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy and Wage Gaps: Evidence from China
highlights.summary: Using panel data for 280 Chinese cities from 2011 to 2023, the study finds that AI pilot zone designation significantly widens wage gaps, with differential effects across skill levels and regions, providing causal evidence on AI's distributional wage impact.

highlights.title: Competition in Generative AI: Evidence from Consumer Demand
highlights.summary: Using transaction-level card data covering 174 million consumers and 114 billion transactions, the study documents paid GenAI service adoption patterns through April 2026, providing direct demand-side measurement of consumer GenAI adoption at scale.

highlights.title: Training Your Replacement: Worker Incentives and the Pace of Automation
highlights.summary: This NBER working paper models the strategic dynamic in which firms ask workers to train AI systems that will displace them, finding that workers' ability to shirk or obstruct slows automation pace and that dismissal threats lose effectiveness when training completion ends the job.

highlights.title: The hidden costs of technological change: investigating pathways through which highly automatable jobs undermine workers' health in Germany
highlights.summary: Peer-reviewed study links high job-automation exposure to measurable health deterioration in German workers, identifying job insecurity and reskilling pressure as mediating pathways, with displacement risk quantified across automation-exposure quintiles.

highlights.title: Indeed Hiring Lab: US Labor Market Snapshot — October 2026
highlights.summary: Indeed's October 2026 monthly snapshot tracks US job postings, wages, unemployment, and openings, providing near-real-time labor demand indicators including any AI-related occupational posting trends through mid-October 2026.

highlights.title: The Occupational Ladder: Implications for Life-Cycle Wage Dynamics
highlights.summary: NBER working paper decomposes how occupational ladder rungs drive average wage growth and the fanning-out of wages over workers' life cycles, providing structural estimates of occupation-level wage premia relevant to modeling AI-driven occupational resorting.

highlights.title: AI-driven 'new migrants': skill-spatial mismatch and out-migration intention
highlights.summary: Using China Migrant Population Dynamic Monitoring Survey and patent data across 250 cities (2014–2018), the study quantifies how local AI intensity drives skill-spatial mismatch and increases out-migration intentions among displaced workers, linking automation exposure to geographic labor reallocation.

highlights.title: Artificial Intelligence, Automation, and the Sustainability of Social Security Systems: The Technological Unemployment Premium Proposal
highlights.summary: Integrative literature review quantifies projected contribution shortfalls in social-security systems under varying technological unemployment scenarios driven by AI and automation, synthesizing displacement rate estimates from the existing literature.

highlights.title: The Twin Transition and Labor Market Transformation: A Conceptual Framework for AI-Enabled Green Growth
highlights.summary: Conceptual framework distinguishes green structural reallocation from AI-driven within-workplace task reorganization, arguing both transitions interact to reshape occupational demand and authority structures in ways standard labor models miss.

highlights.title: Chicago Fed Working Papers: Making Sense of Labor-Market Indicators Amid Data Imperfections
highlights.summary: Chicago Fed working paper addresses measurement challenges in current US labor-market indicators, relevant to benchmarking AI-displacement signals against imperfect official data.

highlights.title: Chicago Fed Working Papers: The Chicago Fed Labor Market Indicators — Bridging the Gap with Alternative Labor Data
highlights.summary: Chicago Fed working paper introduces alternative data sources to supplement official BLS labor market indicators, providing a methodological bridge for incorporating non-traditional employment signals relevant to AI impact tracking.

themes: Managerial AI sentiment and earnings-call signals are emerging as leading indicators of employment and wage outcomes, ahead of conventional survey measures
Causal evidence on AI's wage-gap effects is accumulating from quasi-experimental city- and region-level policy variation, primarily in China
Worker strategic behavior (shirking, obstruction) during AI training transitions is gaining formal modeling attention, with implications for automation speed forecasts
